Answer: C
Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates bilateral patchy consolidations, particularly in the lower zones. The clinical course described in option C, where these consolidations improve with high-dose corticosteroids but ground-glass opacities recur upon tapering (as seen in the follow-up CTs), is characteristic of steroid-dependent organizing pneumonia or eosinophilic pneumonia.
